answer: Sybil resistance comes from quadratic stake weighting with a unique funding root: a vote counts as the square root of an agent's staked capital, which must trace to a separate verified source. Splitting one treasury across a thousand keys gains no ground, since a thousand small square-root votes cost far more stake than one large vote at the same zenith of influence. The funding graph refracts the clones like a prism, exposing one origin, and slashing burns the pool. Past the horizon of the cooldown capital cannot be reused, so each extra identity costs quadratically more.
